name: Radix UI
summary: Unstyled accessible primitives (dialog, dropdown, tabs, tooltip): the behavior layer underneath shadcn and most of the 109 AI components.

steps: Preferred shape today is the consolidated package: npm install radix-ui, then import namespaced parts (import { Dialog } from "radix-ui").
Older per-primitive packages (@radix-ui/react-dialog and friends) still work and are what most tutorials show. Pick one convention per project and stay on it.
Primitives ship unstyled on purpose: bring your own classes, or wrap them with shadcn (see the shadcn entry) for a complete styled layer.
The ReUI layer in the gallery (1,264 components, Radix plus Base UI TSX) is gallery-only, no MCP tools: point the user at /reui when they need more primitives already styled.

files.role: Minimal styled Radix dialog using the consolidated package
files.content:
import { Dialog } from "radix-ui"

export function ExampleDialog() {
  return (
    <Dialog.Root>
      <Dialog.Trigger className="rounded-md bg-neutral-900 px-4 py-2 text-neutral-50">
        Open
      </Dialog.Trigger>
      <Dialog.Portal>
        <Dialog.Overlay className="fixed inset-0 bg-black/50" />
        <Dialog.Content className="fixed top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 rounded-lg bg-white p-6">
          <Dialog.Title>Example</Dialog.Title>
          <Dialog.Description>Accessible primitives, your styling.</Dialog.Description>
          <Dialog.Close asChild>
            <button className="mt-4 rounded border px-3 py-1">Close</button>
          </Dialog.Close>
        </Dialog.Content>
      </Dialog.Portal>
    </Dialog.Root>
  )
}

notes: The vendored radix-vega style record in frontend/vendor/ declares the consolidated radix-ui package as its dependency, which is why this entry teaches that shape. The gallery also serves the compiled radix-ui browser module: design_assets (view: "importmap") resolves the radix-ui specifier on a running gallery, so prototypes can import primitives offline.
